The statement delivers a 25 bp “insurance” easing to 1.50–1.75% and adds T-bill purchases and repo operations to keep reserves ample, signaling supportive financial conditions despite weak business fixed investment and exports with inflation below 2%. Investment literature emphasizes its sensitivity to financing costs and internal funds; cutting rates and easing liquidity can mitigate financing frictions and bolster capex and inventories (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein 1994; liquidity effect). In New Keynesian models, inflation dynamics depend on expectations and the output gap; with market-based inflation compensation low and inflation running below target, modest accommodation is consistent with stabilizing inflation toward 2% without large overheating risks (Galí and Gertler 1999; Woodford 2003; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005). The broader monetary policy literature supports that lower policy rates and reliable operating procedures transmit to output and investment via the interest-rate channel (McCallum and Nelson 1999; Romer and Romer). Two dissents and the noted capex/export softness temper the outlook, but the net signal for growth and financial conditions is cautiously positive.
